q: What is the difference between continuous delivery and continuous deployment?
options: Delivery keeps every change release-ready with a manual approval; deployment releases every passing change automatically
Delivery is only for mobile apps
explain: The manual approval step before production is the difference.

q: In GitHub Actions, where do workflow files live?

options: One after another in file order
In parallel unless you use needs:
explain: Add needs: [jobA, jobB] to make a job wait for others.

q: Why do files from one job not exist in the next job?
options: Each job runs on a fresh machine; share files with artifacts
explain: Upload an artifact in one job and download it in another.

q: What does a build matrix do?
options: Runs the same job for several combinations (Node versions, OS) in parallel
explain: matrix: { node: [18, 20, 22] } creates one job per value.

q: Best cache key for npm dependencies?
explain: The key changes only when dependencies change, so the cache is reused safely.

q: How should you tag Docker images for deployment?
options: With the commit SHA (and optionally a version)
explain: SHA tags are traceable and make exact rollbacks possible.

q: How do you make a production deployment require a human approval in GitHub?
options: Use an Environment with required reviewers
explain: Jobs that target a protected environment pause until reviewers approve.

q: Which is safest for giving a workflow access to AWS?
options: A long-lived access key stored as a secret
OIDC with a role to assume (short-lived credentials)
Putting the key in the YAML
explain: OIDC avoids storing long-lived cloud keys.

q: What does a canary release do?
options: Sends a small share of traffic to the new version first and watches metrics
explain: If the canary is unhealthy you roll back with few users affected.

options: Instant rollback by switching traffic back
explain: The old environment stays running until you are sure; the cost is double capacity.

options: Git as the source of truth; a controller (Argo CD, Flux) pulls and applies the desired state
explain: Deploy and roll back by merging or reverting commits.

q: Which is NOT one of the four DORA metrics?
explain: The fourth is time to restore service.

q: Branch protection with required status checks is used to…
options: Block merging until the pipeline passes (and reviews are done)
explain: A workflow alone cannot stop a merge; the required check enforces the gate.
